exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 11–20, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The set of all affine combinations of points in a set $$S$$ is called the affine hull of $$S$$ .﻿
(T/F) If $$S = \left\{ \textbf{x} \right\}$$ , then $$\text{aff} S$$ is the empty set.

(T/F) If $$\{\textbf{b}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{b}_{k}\}$$ is a linearly independent subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ and if $$\textbf{p}$$ is a linear combination of $$\textbf{b}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{b}_{k}$$ , then $$\textbf{p}$$ is an affine combination of $$\textbf{b}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{b}_{k}$$ .﻿
(T/F) A set is affine if and only if it contains its affine hull.
(T/F) The affine hull of two distinct points is called a line.
(T/F) A flat of dimension $$1$$ is called a line.
(T/F) A flat is a subspace.
(T/F) A flat of dimension $$2$$ is called a hyperplane.
(T/F) A plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ is a hyperplane.
(T/F) A flat through the origin is a subspace.

Suppose $$\{\textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3}\}$$ is a basis for $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ . Show that $$\text{Span} \left\{ \textbf{v}_{2} - \textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{3} - \textbf{v}_{1} \right\}$$ is a plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ . [Hint: What can you say about $$\textbf{u}$$ and $$\textbf{v}$$ when $$\text{Span} \left\{ \textbf{u},\textbf{v} \right\}$$ is a plane?]

Show that if $$\{\textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3}\}$$ is a basis for $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ , then $$\text{aff} \left\{ \textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3} \right\}$$ is the plane through $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ , and $$\textbf{v}_{3}$$ .﻿

Let $$A$$ be an $$m \times n$$ matrix and, given $$\textbf{b}$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ , show that the set $$S$$ of all solutions $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$$ is an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .﻿

Let $$\textbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$$ and let $$k \in \mathbb{R}$$ . Prove that $$S = \left\{ \textbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}:\textbf{x} \cdot \textbf{v} = k \right\}$$ is an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .﻿
Choose a set $$S$$ of three points such that $$\text{aff} S$$ is the plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ whose equation is $$x_{3} = 5$$ . Justify your work.
Choose a set $$S$$ of four distinct points in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ such that $$\text{aff} S$$ is the plane $$2x_{1} + x_{2} - 3x_{3} = 12$$ . Justify your work.

Let $$S$$ be an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ , suppose $$f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ is a linear transformation, and let $$f(S)$$ denote the set of images $$\left\{ f\left( \textbf{x} \right):\textbf{x} \in S \right\}$$ . Prove that $$f(S)$$ is an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ .﻿

Let $$f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ be a linear transformation, let $$T$$ be an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ , and let $$S = \left\{ \textbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}:f\left( \textbf{x} \right) \in T \right\}$$ . Show that $$S$$ is an affine subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .﻿
